newsitem.title: USA: CSCE cocoa called to open flat to $5 a tonne lower.
newsitem.headline: CSCE cocoa called to open flat to $5 a tonne lower.

text.p: CSCE cocoa futures were called to open unchanged to $5 per tonne lower Friday on the heels of a weak performance in London overnight, traders said.

LIFFE cocoa futures were mainly lower early, but benchmark September managed to hold above key chart support at 1,000 stg a tonne. At the midday break, September was down nine stg at 1,006 stg, traded 1,010 to 1,002 stg. December dropped eight stg to 1,042 stg.

Thursday, New York cocoa futures ended broadly lower in local-dominated trading. September settled down $25 at $1,513 a tonne after ranging between $1,542 and $1,510. Second-month December closed down the same at $1,560, while the back months also finished down $25.

On the charts, traders pegged September nearby support at yesterday's low of $1,510, with psychological support noted at $1,500. Subsequent downside hurdles were put at $1,485 and $,1475. On the upside, resistance was seen at $1,547-$1,550, followed by a gap between $1,561 and $1,570.
